s1.syndrome_frame: Severe respiratory infection with subsequent ocular involvement
salient_findings: Blurred vision and redness in one eye
Relative afferent pupil defect and central scotoma
key_facts: Recent close contact with a fatal case
No relevant medical history
Developed ocular symptoms on day 2 post-admission
Best-corrected visual acuity was +2 logMAR (hand movement) OD
Relative afferent pupil defect in the right eye
Central scotoma in the right eye
Impaired color and contrast vision in the right eye
Mild anterior chamber inflammation in the right eye
Noticeable pupillary edema in the right eye
2 peripapillary hemorrhages in the right eye
Mild vitreous inflammation in the right eye
Retinal vessel narrowing in the inferior retina of the right eye
Normal complete blood cell counts
Normal serum angiotensin-converting enzyme levels
Negative results for syphilis, HIV, Toxoplasma gondii, and Borrelia serologies
Positive nasopharyngeal swab RT-PCR for SARS-CoV-2
Negative CSF SARS-CoV-2 RT-PCR

differentials: Acute posterior multifocal placoid pigment epitheliopathy
per_call: Acute posterior multifocal placoid pigment epitheliopathy

raw.rationale: The patient's recent close contact with a fatal case, development of severe bilateral pneumonia, and positive nasopharyngeal swab RT-PCR for SARS-CoV-2, along with the onset of ocular symptoms, suggest a strong link between COVID-19 and the patient's condition.

rejected.label: Retinal vasculitis
rejected.why: While the patient has retinal vasculitis, it is likely a complication of the primary condition rather than the primary diagnosis itself.

rejected.label: Optic neuritis
rejected.why: The patient's symptoms, such as central scotoma and impaired color vision, are consistent with optic neuritis, but this is likely a manifestation of the underlying disease rather than the primary diagnosis.

rejected.label: Varicella-zoster virus retinitis
rejected.why: The patient's negative IgM and very weakly positive IgG for VZV suggest that VZV is unlikely to be the primary cause of the patient's condition.

rejected.label: Herpes simplex virus retinitis
rejected.why: The patient's negative IgM and very weakly positive IgG for HSV suggest that HSV is unlikely to be the primary cause of the patient's condition.
